pros: Fundamental graph primitive with many applications
Multiple algorithm variants for different graph sizes
Forward algorithm achieves optimal O(E^(3/2)) complexity
Provides basis for computing clustering coefficients
Can be computed incrementally for dynamic graphs
Useful for identifying cohesive subgroups in networks
cons: Worst-case O(V³) for dense graphs (near complete graphs)
Memory intensive for large graphs with high average degree
Does not capture larger cycles (4-cycles, 5-cycles, etc.)
Directed triangle detection more complex than undirected
Exact counting infeasible for very large dense graphs
Sensitive to graph topology (power-law vs random vs regular)
Approximation may be necessary for billion-scale networks
